adversarial|apps/api/src/analytics/servi.title: Sustained traffic outpaces retry-record expiry cleanup
adversarial|apps/api/src/analytics/servi.why_it_matters: The collector accepts traffic independently across source and visitor quotas, but the scheduler removes only 500 expired events every five minutes. At 200 accepted page entries per minute (for example 200 independent visitors each opening one page), 1,000 records expire between runs while only 500 are removed. The expired backlog grows by 500 each cycle, retaining event-level visitor/product/release associations far beyond the documented two-hour retry window and eventually consuming database capacity. The deliberate per-query batch bound is reasonable, but there is no continuation or draining mechanism to keep retention bounded.
evidence: apps/api/src/analytics/service.ts:60:     (SELECT rowid FROM traffic_event_dedup WHERE expires_at <= ? ORDER BY expires_at LIMIT 500)`,
apps/api/src/index.ts:31 calls cleanupTraffic once per non-backup scheduled invocation; apps/api/wrangler.jsonc:32 configures that invocation every five minutes.
apps/api/src/analytics/protection.ts keys quotas separately by source and visitor; no global ingestion ceiling restricts all traffic to the cleaner's 100 records/minute capacity.
apps/api/src/analytics/service.ts:52 sets expires_at to now + two hours, while migration 0039 retains visitor_digest, product_id and release_id on each dedup row until deletion.

apps/api/test/analytics/traffic.test.ts:317-330 verifies only that one cleanup leaves one of 501 expired rows; it does not exercise scheduled backlog continuation. docs/progress/2026-09-29-cda-runtime-setup.md:17 describes retry records as lasting two hours.
adversarial|apps/api/src/analytics/servi.suggested_fix: Keep bounded deletion batches, but drain or enqueue continuation while expired rows remain, using a bounded execution budget and a continuation mechanism when that budget is exhausted. Add a focused scheduler/cleanup test with several batches proving backlog progress exceeds supported ingestion and aggregates remain intact.

reliability|apps/storefront/app/utils/tr.title: Bound traffic requests so one stall cannot stop collection
reliability|apps/storefront/app/utils/tr.why_it_matters: Integration point without a timeout: both identity and event requests use native fetch without a deadline, while every subsequent route entry waits on the same pending promise. If an identity response, response body, or event response stalls, the affected tab stops collecting every later route entry until that request eventually settles. An identity stall additionally holds the cross-tab Web Lock supplied by the plugin, preventing other tabs from initializing traffic. Shopping remains usable, so this loss is silent in the dashboard rather than a visible page failure.
evidence: apps/storefront/app/utils/traffic.ts:15-22: identity fetch and response.json() are awaited without an AbortSignal or deadline.
reliability|apps/storefront/app/utils/tr.suggested_fix: Give identity acquisition (including JSON body consumption) and each event attempt a finite AbortController deadline, clearing the timer in finally. A 10-second deadline is a defensible default for optional analytics. Let the existing catches release the queue and Web Lock after timeout, preserve the identical event ID/body for the existing bounded retry, and add a focused stalled-request test proving later visits can proceed.
